title: IT shares fall for 6th straight session; Coforge, Infosys, TCS fall up to 6%- Moneycontrol.com
text:
My Alerts Go Ad-Free Follow us on: Shares of Coforge fell after the sudden resignation of Chairman OP Bhatt   September 09, 2026 / 11:28 IST             IT index slid 3% on September 9 with constituent Coforge tumbling up to 6% after Chairman Om Prakash Bhatt resigned following concerns raised by an internal audit over the company's board evaluation process. Bhatt resigned after an internal audit into a board evaluation found concerns, including that material information about his own performance had not been fully disclosed to the board. Bhatt, who previously served as chairman of State Bank of India, was appointed chair of Coforge's board in 2024 with a term due to finish in April 2027. An audit into the board evaluation process and the resulting report, which were handled under Bhatt's guidance, identified concerns about how the report "had been dealt with and presented to the board", the company said. This included concerns that material information about Bhatt's own performance had not been fully disclosed to the board. At 10 am on September 9, Nifty IT index was trading 3% lower with  Coforge  leading losses. Infosys, Tech Mahindra were among top Nifty losers by declining 3.6% and 3.3%, respectively. The sectoral index fell for sixth straight session, falling over 10% during the same period. "Today's IT selloff wasn't about any one name; it was the sector carrying the market's worries for it. Nifty IT fell close to 3% while the Nifty 50 held up far better near 23,500, and that gap tells you where the nerves are. Infosys took the sharpest cut at around 3.3%, with Tech Mahindra and HCL Technologies each off roughly 2.6 to 2.7%. Crude above 97 dollars and revived Fed rate hike bets set the tone, but the real sting was the expanded 9-11 visa fee that kicked in today. Paying 4,000 dollars on every H-1B extension and 4,500 on every L-1 turns an occasional charge into a running annual bill for firms built on onshore Indian engineers, and the Street is reading that straight into margins in a sector already down roughly 24% this year," said Nitant Darekar, Research Analyst at Bonanza. Coforge did not elaborate on the specific nature of the information about Bhatt's performance that had not been disclosed to the board. The board raised its concerns with Bhatt and was evaluating his response when Bhatt tendered his resignation on September 8. "The immediate change in leadership creates a degree of governance uncertainty, particularly as the resignation stems from concerns identified through an internal audit rather than being a routine transition," ICICI Securities said in a note. In his resignation letter, which was included in the regulatory filing, Bhatt maintained that he had acted in good faith. "I believe that continuing on the Board while there remains a disagreement considering the characteristics of my good faith actions in the Board evaluation process would not be conducive to the effective functioning of the Board," Bhatt said in the letter. Coforge named Vivek Sharma, a non-executive independent director, as interim chair until January 31, 2027.                        Discover the latest  Business News ,  Sensex , and  Nifty  updates.
